topics.label: Lecture opening and cancer therapy objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students to the lecture and states what they should learn about cancer treatment.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: Both approaches directly treat a tumor mass, with surgery removing it and radiotherapy damaging tumor-cell DNA.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy: mechanisms, benefits and limitations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cytotoxic drugs damage cancer cells, their clinical benefits, and the toxicity and resistance that limit them.

topics.label: Targeting hormone dependence in breast and prostate cancers
topics.groupedBecause: Both examples block hormone signaling on which particular cancers depend for continued growth.

topics.label: Exploiting cell-cycle checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: Both approaches exploit missing checkpoint controls to make cancer cells vulnerable to radiation damage or viral replication.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how blocking PARP exploits BRCA-related DNA repair defects to selectively kill cancer cells.

topics.label: Genome-guided targeting of oncogenic drivers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics connect the idea of oncogene addiction and genome-guided treatment to kinase inhibitors that target activated oncogenic drivers.

topics.label: Resistance and limitations of kinase inhibitor therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show why kinase-inhibitor responses can be difficult to sustain as tumor adaptation and treatment limitations turn cancer control into chronic management.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes antibodies that recognize cancer-associated surface proteins to block receptors or recruit immune-mediated cell killing.

topics.label: Antibody–drug conjugates for targeted cytotoxic delivery
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic focuses on using an antibody to deliver a cytotoxic drug into cells bearing its target.

topics.label: Evidence for immune surveillance in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines observations and studies bearing on whether the immune system naturally protects against cancer.

topics.label: Immune checkpoint inhibition and neoantigen response
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how checkpoint blockade can reactivate T cells and how tumor neoantigens can shape the response.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells toward cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: Both approaches bring T cells into targeted contact with cancer cells so that the T cells can attack them.

topics.label: Challenges and personalization in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic summarizes treatment limitations and the need to match therapies to patients using biomarkers and cancer profiling.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends and the role of prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers how prevention and earlier diagnosis contribute to changes in cancer outcomes over time.

topics.label: Future cancer treatment and the choice between proven and experimental therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider future treatment priorities and the dilemma of testing new therapies when established treatments already have strong results.
